failure_inputs: VERIFIED in isolation with a standalone harness reproducing the exact `flip`/Str.global_replace snippet: `"Search (0 < x -> x <= y)%R."` -> `"Search (0 < x -< x <= y)%R."` and `"Search (Rle_lt_trans -> foo)%R."` -> `"Search (Rle_lt_trans -< foo)%R."` — the ordinary implication arrow "->" contains '>' and "-> " matches the "> " needle, so ANY query containing an implication (extremely common Rocq syntax) that legitimately returns zero hits gets its arrow corrupted into the invalid token "-<" before being silently substituted in as the tool's result, typically surfacing as a confusing "search syntax error" instead of the correct "no lemmas found; try a more general pattern" message.

Even for genuine inequality queries, `String.contains q '>'` triggers the flip for ANY '>' anywhere in the string (not just as the head relation), so a query like `Search (foo_gt_compat _ _)%R.` (a bare name fragment/identifier containing no comparison at all but happening to embed no '>' — counter-example aside, any name fragment containing a literal '>' character, or a pattern with an unrelated later '>' e.g. inside a nested subterm) would also spuriously retry with a corrupted copy.
search_tool_inequality_flip_string_surge.replacement_sketch: Either guard the flip to skip entirely when the query contains "->" (String.contains via a substring check for "->"), or restrict replacement to a leading relation token only (e.g. only when the ENTIRE pattern after "Search " starts with `_ <op> _`), or drop the string-rewrite approach and instead issue TWO structurally-independent Search calls built from parsed constr_pattern components. No single existing runtime call substitutes for "flip a comparison operator embedded in free-form Search-query text" — plainly this is a case where manipulating source text is the right shape (the text IS the artifact being resubmitted); the defect is that the specific replace is unguarded against "->", not the choice of mechanism A itself.

failure_inputs: Reproduced on the LIVE server: `raw search {"query": "(_ > 0 -> False)"}` — legitimate zero-hit query, gets flipped to `(_ < 0 -< False)`, and the tool reports "search syntax error: Syntax error: [term] expected after '-' (in [term])." instead of "no lemmas found; try a more general pattern"

rocq_agent_session:strip_comments_asymme.approximates: the file's real token stream with comments removed — exactly what Rocq's own lexer computes as a side effect of tokenizing, correctly, in both directions.

rocq_agent_session:strip_comments_asymme.replacement_sketch: Tokenize with CLexer.Lexer (or Procq's lexer built on it) and reconstruct comment-stripped text from the token stream instead of a hand-rolled state machine that is asymmetric between the two contexts (inside-comment vs inside-code) it claims to handle uniformly. Minimal fix short of that: make the depth=0 branch string-aware the same way the depth>0 branch already is.

failure_inputs: "Time Qed." (or "Time Defined."/"Time Save.") — is_qed_like returns false since the trimmed text starts with "Time" not "Qed", so the short timeout_s is used for what may be the most expensive step in the sentence (kernel type-check); a Qed that legitimately needs qed_timeout_s can now spuriously time out because the agent wrapped it in Time.
"(* close *) Qed." — String.trim strips only whitespace, not comments, so a leading comment defeats the prefix check the same way.
driver:is_qed_like.replacement_sketch: At line 239, vc : Vernacexpr.vernac_control is already in scope. Replace `if is_qed_like text` with `match Vernac_classifier.classify_vernac vc with Vernacextend.VtQed _ -> qed_timeout_s | _ -> timeout_s`. This also correctly handles Time/Fail/Redirect-wrapped Qed/Defined/Save since the classifier inspects the parsed command, not the surface text.

driver:uninterruptible_re.what_it_does: Str.search_forward for the substrings vm_compute/native_compute/vm_cast_no_check/native_cast_no_check anywhere in sentence text, to decide whether to run the fork-probe safety net before real execution.
driver:uninterruptible_re.approximates: Whether executing this sentence will invoke the kernel's VM/native reduction machinery -- the actual thing that can diverge without hitting Control.timeout's interrupt checkpoints.
failure_inputs: "apply vm_compute_correct." -> the substring match fires (verified empirically) purely because an identifier happens to contain "vm_compute", triggering an unnecessary fork()+pipe()+waitpid() probe for a sentence that never calls vm_compute

`Ltac fast := vm_compute.` invoked later as `fast.` -> the regex does NOT fire (the calling sentence's text never mentions vm_compute), so the safety net is silently absent for the exact indirection case it exists to catch -- this is not a text-parsing bug but an inherent limit of source-level heuristics (no static analysis can predict what an Ltac call will unfold to without running it)
driver:uninterruptible_re.replacement_sketch: No typed pre-execution API can substitute (predicting reduction strategy requires unfolding tactics/notations, i.e. actually executing), so text-scanning is justified here. The available fix is local: the current pattern has no word-boundary check, so an identifier-substring false positive is avoidable with a manual is-identifier-char boundary test around each match (OCaml's Str has no \\b).

If kept as text scanning, loop over ALL `coq.theory` occurrences (repeat search_forward from the end of the previous match, catching Not_found to stop) instead of stopping after the first, and bound each `(name ...)` search to that stanza's own closing paren rather than "anywhere later in the file".

walks and stat()s EVERY .vo under ALL load-path dirs on every cached exec_text call (open/check/build), including .vo files never Required by this session -- an edit to an unrelated, never-loaded .vo in a large project (e.g. hundreds/thousands of .vo files) still triggers a full cache wipe
